S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry about multiple domains of life that is difficult to control and occurs more days than not for at least six months, accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as tension, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and difficulty concentrating. The worries are typically about everyday matters (e.g., work, health, finances, family) and are disproportionate to actual circumstances, causing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. Onset is often gradual, with many patients describing a lifelong tendency to worry that becomes clinically significant in the context of chronic stressors or life transitions, and the course is usually chronic with fluctuating intensity. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by the diffuse, free‑floating nature of the worries (rather than circumscribed fears), the broad range of concerns, and the absence of discrete panic attacks or primary obsessions/compulsions as the central feature.

patient.personality: Dulce is a disciplined, nurturing retiree who enjoys structured routines and creative projects, yet sometimes procrastinates and worries about maintaining her independence as she ages.
patient.stressor: Dulce had settled into a satisfying rhythm of volunteering at the senior center, quilting, and taking occasional trips to visit relatives, finding meaning in staying busy after being widowed. About a year ago, she experienced a minor fall and was evaluated for elevated blood pressure and early joint problems, and although the medical issues were manageable, the consultations and new medications made her acutely aware of her vulnerability and the possibility of losing her autonomy. She began to dwell on every ache, appointment, and news story about illness, quietly worrying about becoming a burden to her children and about who would manage the household and family traditions if her health declined. Over the next nine months, these health concerns expanded into broader, persistent worries that made it harder for her to wind down at night, and the disruption to her previously reliable sleep routine, along with increasing daytime fatigue that interfered with her volunteering and church activities, ultimately prompted her daughter to encourage her to see a psychiatrist.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I just can’t sleep through the night like I used to, my mind keeps me awake.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I used to sleep straight through the night, but these days I lie there for an hour or more with my mind racing, then wake up two or three times worrying about my health or the kids and just stare at the ceiling until I finally doze off again, so I’m dragging the next day even if I’ve technically been in bed all night.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: Ever since that fall and the blood pressure business, I find myself worrying all day about everything—if a little twinge in my knee means I’ll end up in a wheelchair, if I’ll forget to pay a bill, if I’ll fall at the senior center, even if my grandchildren will be upset when I can’t host Christmas anymore—things that I know are probably fine but still feel like disasters in my head.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Once the worrying starts, especially in the evenings, it’s like a train I can’t get off—I tell myself to stop, I turn on the TV or pick up my quilting, but the ‘what ifs’ just keep pushing in one after another until I’m exhausted and sometimes even praying out loud for my brain to just be quiet.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.
S058.manifestation: Most days I feel like I’ve got a motor running inside me, my shoulders and jaw clenched, my leg bouncing when I sit in church or at the senior center, and even small noises like the phone ringing make me jump, like I’m braced for some bad news.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: When I’m trying to read my daily devotional or balance the checkbook, I lose my place over and over because my mind drifts off to whether I took my pill, what if I fall in the shower, what if I forget something important, and sometimes I just sit there staring at the page with my head completely blank, not even remembering what I was doing.
